# Low-Voltage (LV) Distribution and White Space Power Delivery {#sec-lv-distribution-white-space-power}

## Technical-Commercial Overview: White Space LV Power & Raceway Economics {.unnumbered}

Within the data center white space, traditional under-floor whip distribution from Remote Power Panels ([RPPs]{.gls key="rpp"}) has largely been superseded by continuous **overhead track busways** rated between $800\text{A}$ and $5000\text{A}$ [@bicsi2024002; @ref04_helonic]. Downstream power delivery routes through dual A/B overhead copper or aluminum busway runs, terminating in plug-in tap-off boxes that feed redundant rack Power Distribution Units ([rPDUs]{.gls key="pdu"}) within each server cabinet [@bicsi2024002; @ref04_helonic].

Furthermore, raceway measurement is strictly governed by physical separation and thermal derating mandates [@bicsi2024002; @ref04_helonic]. Under the National Electrical Code (NEC), IEC 60364, and ANSI/BICSI 002 standards, low-voltage power cables must maintain physical separation from copper and fiber-optic telecommunications pathways to prevent electromagnetic interference (EMI) [@bicsi2024002; @ref04_helonic]. This separation doubles overhead containment requirements relative to standard commercial buildings [@ref04_helonic]. Simultaneously, cable trays must adhere to a strict **40% to 50% maximum cross-sectional fill ratio** to facilitate convective heat dissipation and accommodate future expansion, requiring physical tray dimensions to be $2.0\text{ to }2.5\times$ larger than baseline conductor volumes dictate, as itemized in @tbl-lv-busway-boq [@bicsi2024002; @ref04_helonic].

| Electrical System Package | Primary Unit of Measurement | Standard Measurement Rules & Inclusions | Critical Commercial Risk & Interface Factor |

: Low-Voltage Switchboards, Overhead Busway, Cabling, and Containment BOQ Breakdown {#tbl-lv-busway-boq}

## Main Low-Voltage Switchboards (MLVS) and Power Distribution Units (PDUs): Isolation transformers, static transfer switches (STS), sub-feed breakers

In accordance with RICS [NRM2]{.gls}, Main Low-Voltage Switchboards ([MLVS]{.gls}; $400\text{V}/415\text{V}$ or $480\text{V}$, Form 4b Type 6/7) and floor-standing Power Distribution Units ([PDUs]{.gls key="pdu"} with K-13/K-20 harmonic-mitigating Zig-Zag isolation transformers) are enumerated (`No.`) with full component schedules detailing incoming/bus-tie Air Circuit Breakers ([ACBs]{.gls key="acb"}), outgoing Molded Case Circuit Breakers (MCCBs), Surge Protective Devices (SPDs Type 1+2), and Static Transfer Switches ([STS]{.gls}) [@rics2021nrm2; @bicsi2024002; @ref03_amanengineering].

## Overhead track busway systems: Open-channel busway (800A to 5000A), end-feed boxes, plug-in bus tap-off units, and drop cords

Measuring overhead track busway requires a strict two-part takeoff under RICS NRM2 [@rics2021nrm2; @ref04_helonic]:

1. **Straight Busway Housing (`m`)**: Measured per linear meter along the centerline by bus material (99.9% conductivity ETP copper vs. aluminum), pole configuration ($3\text{P}+100\%\text{N}+50\%\text{PE}$ or $200\%\text{N}$ for high third-harmonic loads), and IP rating (IP54/IP55 in liquid-cooled halls to protect against coolant spray leaks) [@ashrae2023liquid; @ref04_helonic].
2. **Discrete Busway Fittings & Tap-Off Units (`No.`)**: Every end-feed cable tap box, horizontal/vertical elbow, expansion joint section (required every $30\text{–}45\text{ m}$), end cap, and **Plug-In Tap-Off Box** ($32\text{A}, 63\text{A}, \text{or } 100\text{A}$ three-phase with internal MCB/MCCB, revenue-grade Modbus/SNMP branch circuit meter, and IEC 60309 pin-and-sleeve drop cord) must be enumerated as distinct BOQ line items [@rics2021nrm2; @ref26_aginera_takeoff].

## Remote Power Panels (RPPs) and floor distribution: Branch circuit monitoring, transient voltage surge suppressors (TVSS), panelboard schedules

Where raised-floor whip distribution is specified, each RPP ($225\text{A to }800\text{A}$, dual-bus 42- to 84-circuit panelboards) is measured complete with factory-integrated **Branch Circuit Monitoring Systems ([BCMS]{.gls})** (current transformer strips monitoring every individual pole for [EPMS]{.gls}/[DCIM]{.gls} billing and overload trending) and pre-manufactured liquid-tight flexible metal conduit (LFMC) under-floor whips [@bicsi2024002; @ref14_cxplanner].

## Containment and raceway infrastructure: Heavy-duty ladder racks, wire mesh basket trays, and enclosed conduits

Primary feeder routes utilize heavy-duty galvanized or hot-dip galvanized (HDG BS EN ISO 1461) perforated cable trays and NEMA VE-1 Class 20C ladder racks (`m`), while white space fiber and patch distribution utilizes zinc-nickel or powder-coated **wire mesh basket trays** (`m`, color-coded to distinguish System A Power, System B Power, BMS/ELV, and Telecom Fiber) [@rics2021nrm2; @bicsi2024002; @ref04_helonic].

## Physical pathway segregation: Enforcing National Electrical Code (NEC) / local standard separation between power and communications

To satisfy ANSI/BICSI 002-2024 and EN 50174-2 electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) mandates, unshielded communications trays must maintain a minimum $150\text{ mm to }600\text{ mm}$ clearance (depending on total power circuit amperage and metallic divider shielding) from LV power trays and at least $1.0\text{ m}$ from MV feeders [@bicsi2024002; @ref04_helonic]. In congested corridors, this forces multi-tiered Unistrut trapeze hangers ($2\text{- to }4\text{-tier}$ drop-rod assemblies), increasing support steelwork tonnage per linear meter of tray by $40\%\text{ to }60\%$ [@rics2021nrm2; @ref04_helonic].

## Tray sizing economics: Complying with 40%–50% cable fill ratio mandates for thermal dissipation and future expansion capacity

The cross-sectional area occupied by $N$ circular cables of outer diameter $d_i$ inside a rectangular tray of width $W$ and usable depth $D$ is governed by the maximum fill ratio $f_{\max} \in [0.40, 0.50]$ in @eq-tray-fill-ratio, with standard tray selections tabulated across conductor counts in @tbl-cable-tray-fill-calculator [@bicsi2024002; @ref04_helonic]:

$$A_{\text{cables}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \pi \left(\frac{d_i}{2}\right)^2 \le f_{\max} \cdot (W \cdot D) \implies W_{\min} = \frac{A_{\text{cables}}}{f_{\max} \cdot D}$$ {#eq-tray-fill-ratio}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cable-tray-fill-calculator
#| tbl-cap: "Executable Python Calculator: Standard Cable Tray Width Selection under 40% and 50% Maximum Fill Mandates (100 mm Tray Depth)"

import math

def tray_sizing_calculator(
    cable_count=48, cable_od_mm=18.0, max_fill=0.40, depth_mm=100.0
):
    single_area = math.pi * (cable_od_mm / 2.0) ** 2
    total_area = cable_count * single_area
    min_width = (total_area / max_fill) / depth_mm
    standard_widths = [100, 150, 225, 300, 450, 600, 750, 900]
    selected_w = standard_widths[-1]
    for w in standard_widths:
        if w >= min_width:
            selected_w = w
            break
    actual_fill = total_area / (selected_w * depth_mm)
    return total_area, min_width, selected_w, actual_fill

hdr = (
    f"{'Qty':<4} | {'OD':<4} | {'Limit':<5} | {'Area (mm2)':<10} | "
    f"{'Min W':<6} | {'Tray (mm)':<9} | {'Fill'}"
)
print(hdr)
print("-" * len(hdr))
for count in [24, 36, 48, 64]:
    for f_max in [0.40, 0.50]:
        area, min_w, sel_w, act_f = tray_sizing_calculator(
            count, 18.0, f_max, 100.0
        )
        tray_str = f"{sel_w}x100"
        print(
            f"{count:<4} | {18.0:<4.0f} | {int(f_max*100):<4}% | "
            f"{area:<10.1f} | {min_w:<6.1f} | {tray_str:<9} | "
            f"{act_f*100:.1f}%"
        )
```
